checked.comment: Adversarial K-armed bandit. Rewards are in [0,1] and the environment may adapt to past decisions, so adversarial_adaptive is right. INF needs the horizon n (Remark 2), so learner_knows T and K is right.
Stochastic i.i.d. bandit with distributions on [0,1]. MOSS needs the horizon n, so learner_knows T and K is right.
The registry has no MOSS entry, so null is right.
Theorem 4: sup R_n <= 37/(1-1/q) sqrt(qnK). Regret is max_i E[...], a pseudo-regret. The horizon is known.
Theorem 5: sup R_n <= 49 sqrt(nK) over distributions on [0,1].
Theorem 6: R_n <= 23K sum_{Delta_i>0} max(log(n Delta_i^2/K),1)/Delta_i. The expression is mapped correctly.

summary: The extraction is accurate. All three results (Theorems 4, 5 and 6) match the source, including constants, the known-horizon qualifier and the setting assumptions. The claims made without proof (the 15 sqrt(nK) bound and Remark 3) are correctly left out of the results and mentioned only in notes, and the cited results from Theorems 1 and 2 are recorded as the paper states them.
